{{short description|German chemist}}
'''Wolfgang Beck''' is a German [[inorganic chemist]] who contributed to [[organometallic chemistry]] as well. He was a professor at [[LMU Munich]].

Beck received his PhD under [[Walter Hieber]] at the [[Technical University of Munich]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hieber |first1=W. |last2=Beck |first2=W. |title=Über Tricarbonyleisenverbindungen des Typs &#91;Fe(CO)<sub>3</sub>X&#93;<sub>2</sub> (X = S, Se, SC<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>, SeC<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>, SC<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>) |journal=Zeitschrift für Anorganische und Allgemeine Chemie |date=1960 |volume=305 |issue=5–6 |pages=265–273 |doi=10.1002/zaac.19603050504}}</ref> He later moved to LMU Munich. He became emeritus in 2000.

==Research==
Beck published widely on complexes of simple inorganic and organic ligands. One theme was on organometallic derivatives of [[amino acid]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Severin |first1=Kay |last2=Bergs |first2=Ralph |last3=Beck |first3=Wolfgang |title=Bioorganometallic Chemistry - Transition Metal Complexes withα-Amino Acids and Peptides |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |date=1998 |volume=37 |issue=12 |pages=1634–1654 |doi=10.1002/(SICI)1521-3773(19980703)37:12<1634::AID-ANIE1634>3.0.CO;2-C |pmid=29711516 }}</ref> He investigated [[weakly coordinating anion]]s well before the theme was popular.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Beck |first1=Wolfgang |last2=Suenkel |first2=Karlheinz |title=Metal complexes of weakly coordinating anions. Precursors of strong cationic organometallic Lewis acids |journal=Chemical Reviews |date=1988 |volume=88 |issue=7 |pages=1405–1421 |doi=10.1021/cr00089a017}}</ref>

==Recognition==
*Liebig Memorial Medal (Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker)
*Lavoisier Medal for Bioorganometallic Chemistry
